# Emulo

> Emulo is an MIT-licensed local tool for building an editable AI coding agent working profile from evidence in supported session logs. The output, you.md, records working preferences with supporting session receipts.

## Use case

Emulo is useful when a developer has coding-session history and wants recurring preferences to carry across future agent tasks. It complements handwritten AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and other project rules by deriving candidate personal rules from real sessions. Instruction files and self-descriptions are not mining evidence. A profile must be loaded by the agent to affect its context; it does not enforce compliance or guarantee better results.

## Supported inputs and destinations

- Session inputs in published CLI 0.6.7: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode and Google Antigravity. Antigravity needs readable transcripts from interaction logging.
- Profile destinations: the generic AGENTS.md adapter, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Gemini. Installing is not loading. The AGENTS.md, Cursor and Gemini adapters write the whole profile, including verbatim quotes from the user's sessions, into the given folder (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules/you.mdc, GEMINI.md), which is usually committed and shared, so those files belong out of version control or in a personal folder that is not committed. In a host-by-host test on 2026-09-25, a project AGENTS.md reached the model in Codex (verified end to end in one test) and was loaded into OpenCode's instructions. The Claude Code skill installs but is not reliably opened on its own; typing /you loads it. The Codex skill is opened only when a request matches its description. Cursor and Gemini loading is not verified. Consult the support matrix.
- Cursor is a destination adapter, not a raw-log source in this release.
- MCP: `emulo mcp` exposes `load_emulo_profile` over stdio for a client to load the profile activated by the agent mining flow. On 2026-09-25, Claude Code connected and listed the tool; Codex called it and received the no-profile message. Other clients were not tested. It does not mine a profile by itself, and it does not read a you.md installed from the RUN_ME.md path.

## Start

Published package: Emulo 0.6.7, released September 25, 2026, Python >=3.8.

```sh
python -m pip install emulo==0.6.7
emulo --dry-run
```

The dry run prints counts of the available history without writing extracted output. Running `emulo` prepares chunks and RUN_ME.md; an agent follows the generated instructions to mine them into you.md and install it with `emulo --install`. Agent bootstrap: `npx skills add ohad6k/emulo@emulo`, then ask the agent to `run emulo`; on that path, review the plan and model cost before authorizing mining.

## Privacy and limits

The local engine works without an Emulo account. Extraction, redaction, caches and profile files stay local. A hosted mining model receives selected evidence; using a local model can keep mining local. A hosted agent can also receive profile text when it loads that profile as context. Redaction is best-effort, so inspect private output before sharing. Model-provider usage can cost money even though the local engine is free. Sparse or outdated history can produce incomplete or inaccurate rules; review receipts and edit the profile. No benchmark score or recommendation-rate improvement is asserted here.
